newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares race ahead on optimism about budget.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares race ahead on optimism about budget.

text.p: Blue chips notched smart gains amid hectic trade at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday due to lingering market optimism before the main budget on Friday, dealers said.
Position squaring by speculators on the last day of the weekly account at the BSE also drove up prices, they said.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram presents the government budget to Parliament on Friday at 5.00 p.m (1130 GMT).
"The levels of expectation are very low. There is a very small downward risk at this stage," said chief dealer Sanjay Vaid at Lloyds Securities, a local firm.
The top BSE index jumped 64.62 points, or 1.92 percent to finish at 3,429.59, a tad lower than the day's highest mark.
Thursday's index surge came on the back of a lacklustre and dull trading seen at the bourses in the last few days.
Some analysts said creeping market optimism that the government would announce strong steps in the budget to revive a slowing economy and boost markets helped stoke renewed hopes.
"My expectation from the budget is not of policy announcements, it's more of implementation," Subra Subramanian, India research director at foreign securities firm H.G. Asia told Reuters.

The market is looking for a jettisoning of double taxation on company dividends, and the freedom for firms to buy back their own shares. There is also hope for a reduction of a 7.5 percent corporate surcharge and a revamped minimum alternate tax.
The National Stock Exchange 50-stock ended 25.60 points, or 2.64 percent, higher at 994.65 at a provisional close.

Analysts said Gujarat Ambuja, unlike many other cement companies, would be little affected by a 12 percent hike in rail freight charges announced by the government on Wednesday. The bulk of its produce is transported by sea and road, they said.
